editorial:
Imagine two rough-and-tumble cowboys from Montana who decide they have had enough of the ranch life. They pack up and head to Nashville with a wild plan to start their own detective agency. At first, it feels like a total joke, and they are mostly just winging it while trying to fit into the big city. The vibe is light and fun, almost like a buddy comedy where the leads are completely out of their element. You will love watching these fish-out-of-water characters try to navigate the music scene while pretending they know how to solve crimes.

Once they stumble into a real case involving a kidnapped singer and a messy blackmail plot, the movie actually picks up a lot of speed. The chemistry between the leads is great, and the plot keeps you guessing without being too confusing. While the special effects are dated since it is a TV movie from the 70s, the story holds up well.
endingExplained: The duo eventually tracks down the kidnapped singer by following the money trail from the blackmail scheme. After a few close calls and some funny fights, they outsmart the villains and rescue the star. They manage to expose the bad guys to the police, proving they are actually decent detectives. The movie wraps up with the guys realizing that their accidental business is a success, leaving them happily settled in Nashville.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves buddy comedies and old-school mystery stories.
similarMovies: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
